title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults
citation_text: Morton RW, et al. Br J Sports Med. 2018;52(6):376-384. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2017-097608. PMID:28698222.
notes: Breakpoint ~1.62 g/kg/d for FFM gains; protein source (food vs supplement) not a significant moderator in meta-regression. Verified 2026-11-07.

title: International Society of Sports Nutrition Position Stand: protein and exercise
venue: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
citation_text: Jäger R, et al. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2017;14:20. doi:10.1186/s12970-017-0177-8. PMID:28642676.
notes: 1.4–2.0 g/kg/d typical; higher (2.3–3.1) in hypocaloric for LBM retention; food possible, supplements practical. Verified 2026-11-07.

title: A Systematic Review of Dietary Protein During Caloric Restriction in Resistance Trained Lean Athletes: A Case for Higher Intakes
venue: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
citation_text: Helms ER, et al. Int J Sport Nutr Exerc Metab. 2014;24(2):127-138. doi:10.1123/ijsnem.2013-0054. PMID:24092765.
notes: Recommends ~2.3–3.1 g/kg FFM during caloric restriction in lean RT athletes. Verified 2026-11-07.

citation_text: Karakasis P, et al. Metabolism. 2025;164:156113. doi:10.1016/j.metabol.2024.156113. PMID:39719170.
